**MOTH Chess 3.0: Freedom.** A simpler workspace, a fairer and less restrictive fair-play system, a faster-searching MOTH Engine, and new training tools: Opening Explorer, Endgame Intelligence, Player DNA, adaptive Practice, smart game reports and an Engine Lab. It stays free, local-first and in public beta, with no accounts.

## Install or upgrade in Brave
1. Download `moth-chess-v3.0.zip` below and unzip it.
2. Go to `brave://extensions` and turn on Developer mode. Then either press **reload** on your existing MOTH Chess entry after replacing the `moth-chess-dist` folder, or click **Load unpacked** and pick `moth-chess-dist`.
3. Upgrading from 2.x keeps your settings, games, reviews, training data and models. They are migrated automatically (settings schema v3, database v4), and Home confirms the update once. 2.x users start in the **Full** interface; new installs start in **Simple** and get a short welcome tour.
4. On-board analysis needs site access: MOTH icon → **Allow on …** on a Lichess or Chess.com page.

The zip also contains `fair-play/`, the source of the site rules compiled into this build, along with the docs and the changelog.

## What's new
- **Workspace 3.0.** Home, Analyze, Train, Library and Engine Lab replace the old 12-icon rail. Advanced tools sit under *More tools* in Simple mode, engine options are collapsed, and the last section is remembered. There is a new logo and design, Settings are grouped into 6 sections, and the popup is decluttered.
- **Fair play, reworked.** Analysis now also works on **finished games** and **solved or failed puzzles**, but only once the page itself shows that state. It also works on lessons, the board editor and the explorer, alongside analysis boards, studies, practice and bot games. Live, rated, daily and tournament games, timed puzzle modes and any running clock stay blocked, and uncertain states stay blocked. Everything that isn't assistance (board, Library, training, settings, themes) now works on every page. Checks are event-driven, not continuous polling. A disclaimer is shown on Home, in the popup, in Settings and in onboarding.
- **MOTH Engine 3.0.** The search adds a countermove heuristic, history gravity with a malus for quiet moves that failed, logarithmic late-move reductions, futility pruning, "improving"-aware pruning and two-slot hash buckets. The measured results are below.
- **Analysis Studio.** Evaluation graph by move, undo/redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y), an Endgame tab and an exportable game report.
- **Opening Explorer.** Book responses checked by Stockfish (with gambit, trap and mistake tags), the moves from your own games at a position with your score, typical plans, and a personal repertoire with spaced-repetition drills.
- **Endgame Intelligence.** Exact **king + pawn vs king** results from a local table built in the browser, labelled rules for basic mates, Philidor/Lucena and opposite-coloured bishops, pawn races (rule of the square) and 8 training positions. Larger tablebases are not included: they are gigabytes, and the UI says so.
- **Player DNA and Practice.** Your openings, accuracy trend, mistakes by phase, missed patterns and endgame progress, all from your own games. You can reset it. Recommendations, endgame drills that adapt their level, and repertoire drills.
- **Smart game reports** with critical moments, missed chances, strong moves, accuracy by phase and a documented method. Export as Markdown.
- **Play MOTH** from any position or endgame drill, with draw offers.
- **Engine Lab** (Full mode): MOTH vs Stockfish puzzle benchmark, MOTH-vs-MOTH self-play matches (resumable, with PGN export, savable to the Library as training data) and a results history.
- **Reliability.** Control Center, Eco/Standard/Performance profiles, engine recovery with back-off (no restart loops, with a clear message and *Restart engine*), backup and restore with validation, local diagnostic reports you review before sharing, and update notices from GitHub Releases. You can turn update notices off; MOTH never installs anything by itself.
- **Fixed:** revisiting an analysed position could throw an error in the analysis view (present since 2.0). Practice games, latency samples and training runs were exported but not restored.

## Measured
Engine results on a 2-core VM in Node/WASM, same network for both builds:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| A/B vs 2.0 at 20k nodes/move | **+58.5 ± 50.8 Elo** over 120 games (49 W, 42 D, 29 L; LOS 98.8%) |
| A/B vs 2.0 at 40 ms/move | +31.9 ± 52.2 Elo over 120 games (LOS 88.6%). Positive, but **not statistically significant**. |
| Tactics at 100 ms/puzzle | 224/235 (2.0: 225/235) |
| Nodes to depth 8 | −17% |
| Raw speed | −13% |
| Evaluation experiment (pawn threats, connected pawns, rook on 7th) | +4 Elo over 320 games. Not significant, so **not shipped**. |

All of the following ran in GitHub Actions CI on Ubuntu:

- **216 unit tests** pass, and perft is correct on all reference positions.
- **35 browser tests** in Chromium pass.
- **22 browser tests in the real Brave browser** (Brave 156.1.98.63) pass, with the unpacked extension loaded: extension, HUD and fair play, missing engine files, and Play MOTH.

Measured in the CI browser:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Home visible | 450 ms |
| First MOTH line on a middlegame position | 0.6 s |
| MOTH depth 10 | 1.6 s |
| First Stockfish line | 1.1 s |
| Revisiting an analysed position (cache) | 0.27 s |
| JS heap after 20 workspace switches and 5 reloads | 4–6 MB, no growth |
| Idle engine shut down | 10.5 s with a 10 s setting |
| Missing `moth.wasm` | clear message, no restart loop, Stockfish still works |
| Missing network model | MOTH keeps analysing with its classical evaluation |
| Corrupted settings | repaired on start-up |

## Known limitations
- Website adapters and the finished-game and solved-puzzle detection were tested against stand-in pages that follow the sites' markup, not the live sites. If a site changes its markup, MOTH stays blocked (fail closed) rather than unlocking.
- Unpacked extensions never update themselves. MOTH only tells you when a release is out.
- The engines are single-threaded (overlay frames cannot use SharedArrayBuffer). No new evaluation network was trained in this release.
- Player DNA and the reports only become meaningful after several reviewed games.
